speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Resolution, blowups, and projective spectra
summary: After a group-theoretic heading, the notes discuss Hironaka's resolution theorem through the universal property of blowing up, graded algebras and two explicit centers. The algebraic examples occupy P000001--P000003; Dobrushin begins on P000003. The distinction between a symmetric algebra and a Rees algebra matters, and the crossing-center example is not itself a resolution.

speaker: R. L. Dobrushin
title: Canonical Ising coexistence, contours, and a no-return walk
summary: Dobrushin develops the canonical lattice gas, a criterion for phase coexistence through macroscopic density fluctuations, and the contour estimates underlying his 1965 phase-transition paper. A short walk question follows. Signs and the density/specific-volume notation vary between pages, so the modern statements fix one convention. The walk question lacks enough information to identify its probability law uniquely.

speaker: Irving E. Segal
title: Nonlinear wave evolution and geometry of solutions
summary: A preliminary note explicitly dated Thursday 24 September appears on P000007--P000008; the main 28 September exposition starts on P000011. Both develop the nonlinear Klein--Gordon equation as an evolution in a Hilbert space, then its manifold of solutions, tangent equation, symplectic form and canonical quantization. These are linked to Segal's 1964--65 Leray seminar; they are not an unrestricted existence theorem for interacting quantum fields.

speaker: Irving E. Segal
title: Scattering and canonical fields
summary: The short continuation on P000013 mentions renormalization, scattering, generalized probabilities, particle interpretation and equal-time commutators. Several headings state intentions without enough hypotheses for a theorem. The classical wave-operator construction can be identified more precisely than the asserted quantum existence and uniqueness.

speaker: Laurent Schwartz
title: Radon measures beyond local compactness
summary: Starting on P000013, Schwartz compares abstract measures with Radon measures, pushforwards and completions, compactifications, Radon spaces and stochastic path spaces. The argument separates a cylindrical process law from a Radon law on a suitable function space. Several expansive shorthand claims need restrictions on the topology or a countable family of compact sets.

speaker: Laurent Schwartz
title: Hilbert subspaces and positive kernels
summary: The actual mathematical exposition begins on P000018 and continues through P000022, beyond the catalogue span. Hilbert spaces continuously injected into a locally convex space form an ordered cone, identified with positive kernels. Distribution and Sobolev examples explain how this language recovers weak existence theorems. The correspondence was already presented in Schwartz’s 1962 Bourbaki lecture.

speaker: S. G. Gindikin
title: Weil rigidity and group cohomology
summary: The actual note is on P000017, between the Radon discussion and the Hilbert-kernel lecture. Gindikin reports Weil’s local rigidity argument, its cohomological criterion, and a dimension formula for surface groups. The brief nondiscrete-subgroup aside lacks a usable hypothesis list.

speaker: A. Ya. Povzner
title: Thermodynamic potentials and Wigner distributions
summary: After a brief Kostant bibliographic remark, the notes on P000024--P000025 compare canonical and microcanonical thermodynamics and then introduce the phase-space expression now called the Wigner distribution. Temperature factors and concavity signs require care. The Wigner marginals do not make it a positive classical joint probability.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Kushnirenko’s entropy bound
summary: P000023--P000024 reports Kushnirenko’s estimate of measure entropy by hypersurface expansion, with a partition-boundary argument. His short paper was received on 1 October and presented by Kolmogorov on 7 October 1964, before this report; publication followed in 1965. The notebook’s sharper invertible estimate is distinguished from the theorem explicitly proved in that announcement.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Announcement of Thoma’s character theory
summary: A short paragraph on P000025 points to Thoma’s 1964 work on countable groups, including the rational affine group. Kirillov develops the topic at length on 2 November, record 13. The normalized tracial notion of character must be distinguished from an arbitrary irreducible unitary representation.

speaker: Laurent Schwartz
title: Smooth vectors, invariant distributions and fundamental solutions
summary: On P000025--P000028 Schwartz passes from smoothing in representations to Lorentz-invariant distributions and differential equations on groups. The notes distinguish the solvable Lorentz case from the general invariant-solution question and then discuss global fundamental solutions, with a torus obstruction. The latter has both a constant-mode obstruction and a separate small-divisor obstruction.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Thoma characters and representations over different fields
summary: Kirillov reports three 1964 papers of Elmar Thoma, using the affine group over a finite field and over the rationals as examples. The infinite symmetric group and the type-I criterion follow. A question about rational two-by-two matrices leads into a comparison of rank-one character formulae over complex, real, non-Archimedean and finite fields, ending with adeles. The mathematical text begins on P000029 and ends at the top of P000035; the wider catalogue span also contains neighbouring discussions.

speaker: I. I. Pyatetskii-Shapiro
title: Linnik’s lattice points on spheres
summary: P000036 reports Linnik’s use of arithmetic dynamics to distribute integer solutions of \(x^2+y^2+z^2=m\) on the sphere. The fixed splitting prime is visible; the source also warns that some radii have few points. The catalogue assigns the report to 2 November, while the preceding page separately announces Linnik for the 16th. The handwritten parenthesis Ilya Iosifovich resolves the speaker’s otherwise merged initials.

speaker: M. I. Vishik
title: Fredholm index, nonlinear equations, and families
summary: P000035 moves from Fredholm perturbation invariance to nonlinear equations and parameter families. The homotopy claim is meaningful only after specifying the operator space. Catalogue envelopes overlap adjacent records; the item locators identify the actual passage.

speaker: A. Ya. Povzner
title: Statistical-mechanics programme and particle-energy fragment
summary: P000037 proposes Ruelle, Yang--Lee and Kac readings, then sketches a pair-potential minimization claim. The handwritten given-name attribution conflicts with the catalogue; neither a uniform confinement theorem nor its assumptions can be recovered.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Invariant-subspace announcement and Schur positivity
summary: The enthusiastic invariant-subspace announcement on P000037 is followed by Schur positivity. The first records a subsequently retracted claim, not a solution.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Semiclassical transport and caustic phase
summary: The action/Jacobian description is introduced before the caustic phase problem. This foreshadows the 1967 characteristic-class paper; fuller formulas appear on 23 November.

speaker: Yu. V. Linnik
title: Tests, nuisance parameters and analytic ideals
summary: The record passes from sufficiency and randomized tests to similarity, nuisance variances, Bayes-weighted cotests and analytic ideal methods. The closely matching paper was submitted in December 1964.

speaker: E. A. Gorin
title: Gleason problem for the ball algebra
summary: The precise question is coordinate generation of the maximal ideal at the origin, preserving continuity on the closed ball. Comparisons with the disk, polydisc and unrestricted holomorphic division isolate the boundary issue. The ball case is solved.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: WKB geometry, caustics and Morse index
summary: Action and Jacobian transport are developed through caustics, then related to optical phase and the Morse index. The notebook has inconsistent Schrödinger normalizations; modern formulas are explicitly reconstructed.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Phase volume and the fermionic proof of Sturm oscillation
summary: Berezin’s eigenvalue-counting remark precedes Gelfand’s one-dimensional zeros and determinant argument. The latter uses the fermionic ground state; a full implementation appeared in 2018/2020. The notebook’s sign and indexing require correction.

title: February heading and programme
summary: A heading/plan with names and future topics, adjoining 8 February 1965. No separately identifiable mathematical assertion occurs. The contradictory catalogue date label is preserved as an undated plan.

speaker: I. I. Pyateski-Shapiro
title: Congruence subgroups and elementary matrices
summary: The record contrasts the congruence-subgroup property in ranks at least two with the modular group. The main integer-matrix result was already available in 1964. The blanket assertion about rank-one power quotients needs a low-level exception and an orbifold qualification.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Spin-flavour groups and relativistic symmetry
summary: An SU(6) discussion is juxtaposed with the Hermitian-matrix model of Minkowski space and proposed larger symmetry groups. The matrix display needs a semidirect-product correction. Coleman--Mandula later answered a restricted precise version, not every unification programme.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Primary ideals and differential conditions
summary: The algebraic discussion extracts first-order conditions from a square-zero thickening, then considers derivations, localization and formal flow. The notebook itself warns that I and J were interchanged. The correct prime/primary inclusions are indispensable.

speaker: V. P. Palamodov
title: Holomorphic quotients and differential jets
summary: Palamodov represents a primary-ideal quotient by differential data on its zero variety, with locally realizable compatibility. An appended growth estimate is too incomplete to recover its weighted function space.

speaker: A. S. Dynin
title: Elliptic systems, solution sheaves and finiteness
summary: Local differential operators and symbols lead to solution sheaves and finite cohomology, with fine resolutions and compact functional-analytic comparison. The strongest finiteness assertion needs compatibility hypotheses omitted from the note.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Fredholm sheaf questions and broader ellipticity
summary: Gelfand reduces one example to a point and asks about compact perturbations of sheaf maps, infinite-order ellipticity and low-regularity hypoellipticity. Apart from the point case, the operator categories are not specified sufficiently to create definite open problems.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Adams’s vector-fields theorem and real K-theory
summary: Novikov explains the vector-fields-on-spheres theorem through elementary constructions, Bott periodicity, real projective K-theory and stunted projective spaces. The Adams theorem was published in 1962. A factor 6 in the periodicity sentence and an order statement are faithful notebook errors.

speaker: V. P. Palamodov
title: Primary-ideal quotient revisited
summary: P000060 restates the compatible differential-jet realization of a primary polynomial ideal quotient and says Kazhdan obtains it algebraically. It is a recurrence of record 27, not a separate fully specified growth theorem.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Nelson’s commuting differential operators
summary: P000060--P000061 distinguishes essential self-adjointness from formal symmetry and strong commutation from commutation on a core. The punctured genus-four surface is Nelson’s example, already published in 1959.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Simple eigenvalues and countable Lebesgue spectrum
summary: P000062 and the top of P000063 distinguish simple eigenspaces from the continuous spectral multiplicity of toral automorphisms and Bernoulli shifts. The remark that all known Lebesgue examples have countable multiplicity is historical; no explicit Banach problem is posed.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Group actions, spectral reconstruction and cocycles
summary: The actual record runs from P000063 through P000065, beyond the catalogue envelope. It compares compact homogeneous actions, noncompact representations, cocycles and reconstruction. The finite-group reconstruction question has negative examples; several cohomological remarks remain too indefinite to identify.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand; A. Ya. Povzner; F. A. Berezin
title: Proposed future directions
summary: The short programme on P000063 precedes Kirillov physically, though it is record35 in the supplied order. Four directions are named without definite objects or conjectures; they must not be retroactively identified with later named theories.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Moduli of ergodic eigenfunctions
summary: The dated Sinai fragment on P000063 states that a Koopman eigenfunction of an ergodic system has constant modulus. The surrounding pages continue earlier dynamical-system material and begin other speakers; the catalog envelope is retained without attributing all its contents to this fragment.

speaker: V. N. Latyshev
title: Enveloping algebras, Lie ideals and bounded nilpotence
summary: The speaker, named only Viktor Nikolaevich in the handwriting, discusses primitive universal enveloping algebras, the passage from associative to Lie ideals, and a Burnside-type nilpotence assertion attributed to Kostrikin. The catalog identification as Latyshev is retained. Two assertions require correction or cannot be identified with a theorem under the recorded hypotheses.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Weyl algebras with different numbers of canonical pairs
summary: A short intervention attributes to Dixmier the question whether the differential-operator algebras in one and in two variables are isomorphic. This is a comparison of different ranks. Gelfand and Kirillov answered such isomorphism questions in 1966 by an invariant of growth.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Dyson circular ensembles and the logarithmic gas
summary: The talk explains the circular orthogonal and unitary ensembles, their eigenangle densities and a Coulomb-gas interpretation of an empty arc. It then moves from an exact finite-dimensional integral to a continuum free-energy ansatz. The manuscript fails to keep that approximation separate from an exact gap formula.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Grothendieck topologies and arithmetic cohomology
summary: Beginning with finite-field solutions as Frobenius fixed points, Bernstein introduces slice categories, products, coverings and sheaf descent. The title mentions monoidal transformations, but no actual blow-up construction is developed in this fragment. The category of sheaves over a field anticipates Galois cohomology.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A curriculum and a symmetric-space research direction
summary: This is chiefly a planning intervention: subjects needed by seminar participants are listed, alongside a suggestion to extend Dyson\textquotesingle s calculations to symmetric spaces. The item index preserves both the organizational list and the mathematical direction.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Circular gap probabilities and an even sine-kernel determinant
summary: The discussion revisits the cosine-power claim, relates a nearest-neighbor law to derivatives of an empty-interval probability and displays a cosine determinant with a large-gap prediction. Its written exponent and its scaling parameter require explicit critical annotation.

speaker: A. M. Stepin
title: A torsion-group action with continuous spectrum
summary: Stepin answers the preceding dynamical-system discussion with an action of the dyadic torsion group. Finite-order transformations can jointly have a continuous spectral component. His 1966 paper supplies an exact continuation and stronger spectral analysis.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Recovering convex bodies from central sections and shadows
summary: Kirillov explains how central section areas of a symmetric body reduce to integration of an even function over great spheres. He then asks the analogous question for projection areas. The symmetry assumption is essential for both uniqueness statements.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Dvoretzky sections and an incompletely recorded Gromov method
summary: Kazhdan reports a result of Gromov in the setting of Dvoretzky\textquotesingle s theorem. Sphere bundles over Grassmannians and disappearance of low spherical harmonics are proposed as a method. The exact additional hypothesis and representation-theoretic quantifiers are not preserved well enough to equate this with Gromov\textquotesingle s later Banach-conjecture paper.

speaker: R. A. Minlos
title: Gaussian Hermitian matrices, Brownian motion and angles
summary: The actual Minlos fragment is very short: Gaussian entries in a Hermitian matrix, Brownian motion, and a question about angles between subspaces. The modern interpretations are supplied explicitly as reconstructions, without attributing detailed stochastic equations to the handwriting.

speaker: L. D. Faddeev
title: Characteristic determinants, Jost functions and regularized traces
summary: Faddeev moves from a finite-interval Sturm--Liouville characteristic function to half-line and whole-line Jost determinants, then to contour trace identities. The notes mix exact identities with formal diagonal-kernel reasoning. A final Gelfand question asks when traces of commutators vanish.

speaker: S. G. Gindikin
title: Cauchy--Weil formulas and holomorphic Radon transforms
summary: Gindikin begins with the product Cauchy formula and analytic polyhedra, introduces Hefer decompositions and skeleton integrals, then proposes a continuous family of defining functions. The final linear case connects directly to his 1965 holomorphic Radon-transform note, announced to the Moscow Mathematical Society in February.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Čech complexes and derived sheaf cohomology
summary: Bernstein reviews descent, constructs a Čech complex and maps under refinement, and explains why global sections need derived functors. The example of functions vanishing at two points of the projective line is useful and precise. The attribution of a failure of exactness to taking a direct limit is mathematically wrong and is corrected separately from the underlying cohomological construction.

speaker: Paul R. Halmos; I. M. Gelfand; unidentified participant
title: Invariant subspaces, polynomial compactness, unicellular operators and Bishop operators
summary: Halmos surveys invariant-subspace results and gives the elementary proof of the polynomially compact case. The ensuing questions concern invariant-subspace lattices, weighted shifts, a measure version of Volterra integration and Bishop operators. A final intervention sketches the Sz.-Nagy--Foiaş analytic model. The catalog envelope is preserved, but P000090 begins Kohn on 20 September 1965 and is outside this academic year and record.
